title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LC1RE_0LE0LD_1LC0LB_0RA0RF_1RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LC1RE_0LE0LD_1LC0LB_0RA0RF_1RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. It writes a word of blocks 1100 and 10 that grows to the right logarithmically slowly, like a counter. This page lists what has been established.
verdict: The question is open. The run is two binary counters at a hub, counting down on the left and up on the right; the counting rules are proved in Lean, and an accelerated run reaches 3.93·1013 steps without a halt. The overflows, where the counters are laid out again, are not decoded.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 299 cells have been visited and 155 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is F on 1, and F is entered only from E on 1 (0RF): the machine halts exactly when E reads a 1 followed by another 1, E>1 1.

claims.title: Logarithmic growth
claims.text: The tape grows mostly to the right; the time to reach a new rightmost cell grows by a roughly constant factor per cell (cell 50 at step 1,089, cell 350 at step 16,667,114,039); 359 cells after 18,417,187,404 steps, no halt.

claims.title: What the tape is
claims.text: Read as words a = 1100 and b = 10 (tools/c/tokrun.c), the tape is a string over a, b and single 1s, a counter-like word whose front changes at every pass and whose back is a long regular tail (1 b^2)^n that grows by one unit now and then. The sibling 1RB0RD_1LC1RE_1LD0LC_0LE0LC_0RA0RF_1RA--- (C and D swapped, two transitions differ) behaves the same way.

claims.title: The counter rules
claims.text: One hub event of the two counters, for every borrow length k and carry length j and every tape beyond the cells shown: borrow (10k + 20 steps), carry0, carry1 and plain.

claims.title: No halt in 3.93·10<sup>13</sup> steps
claims.text: A 25-minute accelerated run (tools/py/bbtools/cjump.py, exact step counts) reached step 39,282,271,415,780 (3.93·1013) with 458 cells visited and no halt. From step 3.9·1013 on the learner finds only short jumps (a layout with a 45-cell hub region), so the run slows to direct speed there.

claims.title: Two binary counters at a hub
claims.text: At the hub turn (E reading 0) each event takes 1 from the left counter and adds 1 to the right; cost 10 steps per left digit changed, 12 per right digit changed, 32 per left separator crossed, plus a constant. When the left counter runs out the hub moves and the layout is rebuilt; the rule of that overflow is not decoded.
claims.where: learned by cjump.py, checked on every event it jumps from

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?

explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. It runs two binary counters at a hub, one counting down and one counting up; an accelerated run reaches 3.93·10<sup>13</sup> steps without a halt.

sections.heading: Two counters at a hub
html: At every visit of one turn of the head (E reading 0) the tape reads as two binary counters back to back, lowest digits next to the hub. Left: 4-cell digits 1001 (1) and 0101 (0), the lowest digit 10 (1) / 01 (0), in stretches separated by the 9-cell word 100110101 that borrows cross unchanged. Right: 5-cell digits 10101 (1) and 10100 (0), the lowest digit one cell (1 is 1), with separator words such as 10010100.

Each visit takes 1 from the left counter and adds 1 to the right. It costs 10 steps per left digit changed, 12 per right digit changed, 32 per left separator crossed, plus a constant, so a long borrow or carry costs a little more and the counting is fast to jump over.

Proved in Lean for every length k of a borrow and j of a carry (lean/Counter.lean):

  • borrow (10k + 20 steps): L 1001 (0101)^k 01 E> 0 0 0 R -> L 0101 (1001)^k 10 E> 0 0 1 R, the left counter borrowing through k digits;
  • carry0 (12j + 22 steps): L 1 0 E> 0 0 (11010)^j 1 1 0 1 0 0 R -> L 0 1 E> 0 (00101)^j 0 0 1 0 1 0 1 R, the right counter carrying through j digits;
  • carry1 (12j + 106 steps): the same beyond a 30-cell stretch that holds a separator, the right counter carrying through j digits;
  • plain (22 steps): L 1 0 E> 0 0 1 1 0 1 0 0 R -> L 0 1 E> 0 0 0 1 0 1 0 1 R, the most frequent short event.

When the left counter runs out the hub moves and the counters are laid out again. Seen so far: the hub turn moved to cells 122, 128, 143, 153, 168, 182, 192 and 202 at steps 3.5·107, 2.1·108, 1.3·109, 4.6·109, 1.6·1010, 1.3·1011, 6.1·1011 and 9.9·1012, each layout lasting 3 to 16 times longer than the one before. That rule is the open part.

A 25-minute accelerated run (tools/py/bbtools/cjump.py, exact step counts) reached step 39,282,271,415,780 (3.93·1013) with 458 cells visited and no halt. From step 3.9·1013 on the learner finds only short jumps (a layout with a 45-cell hub region), so the run slows to direct speed there.

sections.heading: A word that grows slowly to the right
html: The machine grows its tape mostly to the right, each new cell costing a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter. Rightmost cell reached and the step it was first reached (direct run of 2·1010 steps):

Read in the words a = 1100 and b = 10, the tape is a word like a^6 b^14 a 1 b^2 a^3 1 b^4 a^5 … followed by a regular tail (1 b^2)^n. Its front changes at every pass of the head; the rule is not yet known.

sections.heading: What halting would take
html: The only halting transition is F on 1, and F is entered only from E on 1 (0RF): the machine halts exactly when E reads a 1 followed by another 1, E>1 1. It has not happened in 2·1010 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.063).
After 109 steps the tape spans 299 cells (31 left of the start, 262 right), with a density of 1s of 0.518.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Two binary counters at a hub (left counts down, right counts up; counting rules proved in Lean); accelerated run to 3.93·10^13 steps, no halt; overflows not decoded.
